diagnostics.message:
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
null_resource.update_forge_role_trust updates each forge role's trust policy to grant the lambda execution role (arn:...:role/${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator) sts:AssumeRole, but it has no dependency on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda which creates that role. The trust update can run before the trusted lambda role exists, so the relationship should be ordered after the module.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
null_resource.update_forge_role_trust rewrites the forge roles' assume-role trust policies to allow the trust-validator Lambda's execution role to assume them, but it has no dependency on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda, which is the resource that actually creates that IAM role (the trust ARN is hand-built from account_id + prefix). It should be ordered after the module — ideally by referencing the module's real `lambda_role_arn` output instead of reconstructing the ARN.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.update_forge_role_trust updates each Forge role's assume-role policy to trust the trust-validator Lambda role (`arn:aws:iam::...:role/${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator`), which is created by module.forge_trust_validator_lambda. It has no dependency on the module, so Terraform can grant trust before that role exists. It should depend on the module so the Lambda role is created first.
